title: How to Actually Tokenmaxx and Save Millions — Alvin Pane, OutRival
talk_summary: The talk reframes tokenmaxxing as maximizing intelligence per token: instrument traces, measure baseline variance with a ceiling test, then cache, shrink prompts via search, downsize/rout models, and shadow-test changes. It gives a concrete release rule based on paired comparisons and confidence intervals rather than raw prompt-engineering guesswork.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument the shared model client so each attempt is part of a task trace with prompt version, model settings, tokens, latency, cost, tools, and retries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instrument your shared model client so each attempt becomes part of a trace connecting the model calls, tools, and retries

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the current production model multiple times on the same inputs to measure its self-disagreement before judging a cheaper candidate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We took our massive expensive production model and ran it three separate times on the same inputs and compared the answers.
takeaways.numbers: Production self-agreement ~93%, self-disagreement ~7%; cheaper candidate disagreed with baseline 18% before baseline correction.

takeaways.what_they_do: Define input/output contract and scoring function, then use DSPy/GEPA to search prompt space and replace long worked examples with compact rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It stripped out almost all of our long worked examples and replaced them with compact rules.
takeaways.numbers: 51% reduction in instruction tokens with same application contract.

takeaways.what_they_do: Structure prompts so static content sits in a stable prefix, maximizing provider prefix-cache hit rate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: structuring your prompts to maximize your prefix cache rate is a really easy and really effective way to bring down the cost

takeaways.what_they_do: Split large prompts into smaller components: cheap models handle routing or extraction, frontier models only handle heavy reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use a cheaper model to handle something like initial routing or data extraction and only wake up your expensive frontier models for heavy reasoning.

takeaways.technique: Shadow deployment with paired confidence intervals
takeaways.what_they_do: Run old and new versions on the exact same inputs, compare production-vs-production, candidate-vs-candidate, and candidate-vs-production, then require lower confidence bound above zero and check critical categories separately.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you run a massive shadow deployment on the exact same inputs and measure the system from three angles
takeaways.numbers: 443 regressions vs 2,463 improvements (~6 improvements per regression); require lower confidence bound above zero.
